To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a classification of KM methods is proposed that identifies the types of KM practices, (2) coordination theory and Text-based Process Analysis are applied to analyze the coordination requirements for each of the KM methods, and (3) the EKA is proposed as a standard for the design of KMS to support the coordination requirements of KM networks.

(a) a KMS must provide the means to coordinate the different KM methods; (b) the coordination requirements are derived by analyzing KM practices; and (c) these requirements can be incorporated into a KMS by adopting the EKA.
the coordination requirements of knowledge management systems (KMS) for supporting knowledge networks can be identified using Text-based Process Analysis (TPA).
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the coordination requirements for KMS and the implications of these requirements for the design and development of KMS.
the design of KMS to facilitate the sharing of knowledge among different organizational units and to enable the creation of a knowledge network.
understanding the requirements for designing KMS that support knowledge networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this paper provides an in-depth analysis of knowledge management practices, and the requirements for knowledge management systems to support such knowledge practices.
this study identifies a set of coordination requirement for the design of knowledge management systems (KMS) to support knowledge networks, by analyzing four cases representing different KM methods.
the proposed EKA is a standard for incorporating the coordination requirements of knowledge management systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the EKA is a conceptual model that can be used as a framework for designing and developing a KMS, which is the first step in integrating knowledge pockets into a knowledge network.

we propose a set of coordination principles for designing and building KMS that support knowledge networks, and provide a common framework for incorporating these principles in the design and development of new KMS, and for the analysis and redesign of existing KMS.
the design and development of a KMS must be based on a thorough analysis of the knowledge processes that the KMS is intended to support.
The main takeaway from our work is that

coordination requirements can help identify and address structural differences in knowledge processes and software systems, thus supporting the integration of knowledge pockets into knowledge network.
the design of a knowledge network must be based on an understanding of the knowledge practices that will be coordinated and the coordination requirements for each practice.
coordination theory is a useful tool for understanding KM methods and for designing KMS to support knowledge sharing across organizational units and across organizational boundaries.
